page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top with page number 90 at left. Main text in one column of verse lines with headings (centred place names) and marginal notes in the left margin, each beside its verse. Final line "Scythia" right-aligned at foot of text.

main_text.head: Sueui, qui & Alemani.

p.note: Claud.in Eu- tropiú lib.1. Idem de 4. Honorÿ con- sul.

main_text.head: Cimbri,& Teuthones vicini.
main_text.p: Idé ibidem.— latísque paludibus exit Cimbrus.

p.i: Hac & Teutonico quondam patefacta furori Colla catenati vidit squalentia Cimbri.

main_text.head: Cherusci, Saxones, & Bructeri vicini.
main_text.p: Albis fl. Idem de 4. có sul.Honorÿ. Idé ibidem. Catti. Cherusci.—ingentes Albim liquere Cherusci. — venit accola sylua Bructerus Hercynia. Quaeq; domant Cattos, immansuetósque Cheruscos.
main_text.head: Franci.
main_text.p: Idem de bello Getico. Idem de 4. có sul.Honorÿ. Id.m in Eu- trop.l b.1.—pauidóque orantes murmure Franci Procubuere solo. Ante pedes humili Franco, tristíque Sueuo Perfruor, & nostrum video Germanice Rhenum.
main_text.head: Sicambri, Catti, & Cayci vicini.

p.i: Agmina quin etiam flauis obiecta Sicambris, Quaeq; domant Cattos, immansuetósque Cheruscos Huc omnes vertere minas.

p.note: Idem de 4. có sul.Honorÿ. Idem in Eu- trop.lib.1.
p.i: Ante ducem nostrum flauam sparsere Sicambri Casariem.

page.notes: Marginal notes in the left margin are abbreviated citations (Claud. in Eutropii lib. 1; Idem de 4. consul. Honorii; Idem de bello Getico; Albis fl.; Catti; Cherusci; Id.m in Eutrop. l.b.1; Idem in Eutrop.lib.1). Some verse lines are partly damaged; "Ardúus" and "Ardum" at the foot are read as Arduus. The final "Scythia" is printed right-aligned and may be a catchword or heading; it is transcribed as a paragraph.
